tools.name: net_salary
tools.description: Take-home pay for an employee in United States from a gross yearly salary in USD, with 2026 rules: every tax and contribution itemised with its local name, the effective and marginal rate, employer cost and the step-by-step workings. Covers: 2026 federal brackets: single, married filing jointly, head of household; Child Tax Credit with phase-out and refundable part; FICA with the 2026 wage base and Additional Medicare; 401(k) (with 50+ catch-up), HSA and section 125 pre-tax deductions; State income tax 2026 for 12 states incl. NYC with their own married-couple tables, exemptions and credits; Employee payroll programmes: CA SDI, NY PFL and DBL, NJ TDI/FLI/UI, MA and WA PFML, WA Cares.

tools.name: tax_rules_covered
tools.description: The United States rules the calculators apply (2026), the options they take, what is not modelled, and the official sources, for the salary calculators and the full income tax return. Call it before answering a question the other tools may not cover.

tools.name: income_tax_return
tools.description: The complete United States income tax computation for 2026, as on the return. Covers: All five filing statuses; married couples always computed jointly and separately, head of household against single; Standard vs itemized deductions: SALT cap $40,400 with the high-income phase-down, mortgage interest and PMI, charity with the 0.5% floor, medical over 7.5%, the 2/37 limit; 2026 brackets, qualified dividends and long-term gains at 0/15/20%, capital loss limit and carryover, AMT with the 50% exemption phase-out; Child tax credit, credit for other dependents, earned income credit, child and dependent care credit, education credits; and more. Returns the tax, the balance still to pay or to be refunded after taxes already paid, every option the law offers compared, and each step with its legal reference. All amounts in USD; everything is optional, give only what applies. What is not modelled is listed in the result.

tools.name: cross_border_year
tools.description: Estimates the employment income tax in BOTH countries for the tax year in which someone moves from one country to another: residency status in each country by its own rules (India's 182-day financial-year test, US substantial presence and dual-status, UK split year, Dutch migration year, German part-year liability), the income each country taxes, tax before and after relief for tax paid abroad, social contributions, the combined total in euros and a comparison with staying. Covers 19 countries; each country is taxed for its own tax year containing the move date. Returns what is not covered, assumptions, and for researched corridors (India with the Netherlands, US, UK or Germany; Netherlands with Germany or the UK) the forms and deadlines, treaty notes and official sources. Salaries are full-year rates in each country's own currency.

salary_after_move.description: Yearly salary rate in the country you move to, in its currency

home_after_move.description: Where your home and family are after the move; decides the treaty tie-breaker (default new_country; none applies no tie-breaker)

indian_citizen.description: India: you are an Indian citizen (default true)

india_rnor.description: India: not ordinarily resident (non-resident 9 of the last 10 years, or 729 days or fewer in India in 7 years)

us_citizen_or_green_card.description: United States: citizen or green card holder

us_days_last_year.description: Days spent in the US last year (substantial presence test)

us_days_year_before.description: Days spent in the US the year before last

uk_split_year.description: United Kingdom: treat the UK part of the year as resident (split-year treatment); default true

pension_pct.description: Employee pension contribution, percent of salary

return_before.description: Optional full tax return arguments for the country you leave: the same arguments as that country's income tax return tool. Its salary and part-year residence are filled in from the dates; everything else is yours.

return_after.description: Optional full tax return arguments for the country you move to: the same arguments as that country's income tax return tool. Its salary and part-year residence are filled in from the dates; everything else is yours.
